the_ruling_verbatim: aa4463bbd067: exactly yes. an 'employer' has to delatate access to an 'employee'

who owns what?: Yes, this is complex for the librarian. and i don't yet know what to do about it. so for now, the librarian is just allowed access to everything. we will go thru a hardening step as we prep this for sharing.
cross owner reads: my thinking was that as an igor's employer, i would give him access to my db. and then the librarian would set up the permissions for that as the overall owner.
that also means each 'user' (me, you, igor, etc) has their own creds. hence the vault.  i can share my creds with igor without actually sharing my creds and the vault just takes care of managing it.
kind of a permissions model for creds access that everybody can use without being able to see them
now_the_spec_says: Cross-owner access is a store permission, not a bus verb. Each principal holds its own creds; an employer grants an Igor access to its database via the vault; the librarian sets the permission up as overall owner. Until the hardening step, the librarian may access everything.
context: CC's one question on the cast ticket was whether a cross-owner address resolve rides db_domain directly or a bus verb to the owning device. Akien answered with the access model (employer/employee delegation, librarian as administrator, librarian unrestricted for now, a hardening step before sharing) and filed a credential vault idea in the same breath (ideas/, 2026-09-06). Not marked RULED in his message. The conforming files are restated after intake.
